categories.name: Smart Contract Platform
categories.content: Smart contract platforms are usually blockchains that host smart contracts or decentralized applications. Users can interact with different smart contracts on these platforms to perform various actions such as lending and borrowing funds, staking their assets or minting NFTs. Smart contracts are programs that are stored on the blockchain and are automatically executed when certain conditions are met.

categories.name: Layer 1 (L1)
categories.content: Layer 1 serves as the primary and autonomous chain on which transactions are directly executed and confirmed, as well as providing the essential infrastructure for the blockchain network.

categories.name: Proof of Work (PoW)
categories.content: Proof of Work (PoW) is a blockchain consensus mechanism to validate transactions and create new blocks through computational efforts by miners.

categories.name: World Liberty Financial Portfolio
categories.content: The World Liberty Financial portfolio includes purchases made by the World Liberty Financial project. World Liberty Financial is a DeFi project associated with U.S. presidential candidate Donald Trump and his family members.

categories.name: Proof of Stake (PoS)
categories.content: Proof of Stake (PoS) is a blockchain consensus mechanism where validators are selected to create new blocks based on the amount of cryptocurrency they hold and are willing to stake as collateral.

categories.name: Stablecoins
categories.content: A stablecoin is a type of cryptocurrency that is designed to maintain a stable value by being pegged to an external reference, such as a fiat currency.

categories.name: Made in USA
categories.content: Refers to cryptocurrencies that have significant connections to the United States, either through their founding team or company headquarters.

categories.name: USD Stablecoin
categories.content: A USD stablecoin is a type of cryptocurrency that is designed to maintain a stable value by being pegged to the United States dollar.

categories.name: Fiat-backed Stablecoin
categories.content: A fiat-backed stablecoin is designed to maintain a stable value by being pegged to a reserve of fiat currency, such as the US dollar, euro, or other national currencies.

categories.name: Alleged SEC Securities
categories.content:
Tokens and cryptocurrencies alleged to be securities by the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC). 

Note: The labeling of these cryptocurrencies as securities by the SEC doesn't equate to the legal classification till proven in a court.

categories.name: Exchange-based Tokens
categories.content: These tokens are associated with both centralized and decentralized exchanges which share the same purposes such as enjoy discounted trading fees and gain access to exclusive token sales on the exchange. While decentralized exchanges tokens also function as governance as a governance tokens, centralized exchange token does not.

categories.name: Made in China
categories.content: Refers to cryptocurrencies that have significant connections to the China, either through their founding team or company headquarters.

categories.name: Centralized Exchange (CEX) Token
categories.content: These utility tokens are issued by a centralized exchange and can be used for a variety of purposes. Although holders are not able to exercise governance, they still carry many other benefits such as enjoy discounted trading fees and gain access to exclusive token sales on the exchange.

categories.name: MiCA-Compliant Stablecoin
categories.content: Fiat-backed stablecoins that are fully authorized under the European Union's Markets in Crypto-Assets (MiCA) regulation. These assets are issued by regulated entities such as Electronic Money Institutions (EMIs) or licensed credit institutions and adhere to strict European standards regarding 1:1 liquid reserve backing, transparent public auditing, and safeguarded custody to ensure consumer protection and financial stability.

categories.name: CoinList Launchpad
categories.content: CoinList is a platform specializes in compliant token launches for new projects.

categories.name: Decentralized Finance (DeFi)
categories.content: Decentralized Finance, is a financial system that operates without central authorities or intermediaries, using blockchain technology and smart contracts to provide a range of financial services such as lending, borrowing, and trading.

categories.name: Real World Assets (RWA)
categories.content: Real World Assets (RWAs) refer to tangible or physical assets that have value in the real world. The tokenization of RWAs involves representing these assets digitally on a blockchain, allowing for fractional ownership, increased liquidity, and more efficient management and trading of these assets.

categories.name: Meme
categories.content: Meme coins derive their relevance from memes, thriving on hype and picking up momentum as the community grows.

categories.name: Governance
categories.content: A governance token grants its holders the right to influence, vote, or decide on changes to a blockchain protocol, dApp, or DAO.

categories.name: Infrastructure
categories.content: Fundamental systems and networks that support the functioning and development of the technology.

categories.name: Dog-Themed
categories.content: Meme coins which are inspired by dog.

categories.name: Decentralized Exchange (DEX)
categories.content: Decentralized exchanges (DEXs) allow users to trade with one another in a permissionless manner and without any intermediaries.

categories.name: Privacy
categories.content: Privacy category showcases all cryptocurrencies, blockchain networks, and infrastructure protocols designed to protect user anonymity and secure data.

categories.name: Binance Alpha Spotlight
categories.content: Binance Alpha is a platform within Binance Wallet that highlights promising early-stage crypto projects before they potentially list on Binance.

categories.name: 4chan-Themed
categories.content: 4chan-themed coins are tokens inspired by 4chan’s meme culture.

categories.name: Tokenized Private Credit
categories.content: Tokenized private credit refers to the digital representation of economic claims on non-publicly traded debt instruments, such as direct loans to businesses or consumers.

categories.name: Artificial Intelligence (AI)
categories.content: Artificial Intelligence (AI) tokens are cryptocurrencies that power AI-related projects, such as AI-powered portfolio management, image generation, path finding, and more.

categories.name: Elon Musk-Inspired
categories.content: Meme coins inspired by Elon Musk, none of these projects are (necessarily) endorsed or created by Elon Musk.

categories.name: Perpetuals
categories.content: Perpetuals offer traders the ability to take leveraged positions on the price of an asset without owning the underlying asset.

categories.name: Tokenized Assets
categories.content: Tokenized products refers to digital representation of assets on a blockchain platform.

categories.name: YZi Labs (Prev. Binance Labs) Portfolio
categories.content: Protocols and tokens that YZi Labs (Prev. Binance Labs) have invested in.

categories.name: Derivatives
categories.content: Derivatives are financial instruments whose value is derived from an underlying asset (e.g. Crude Oil, Gold, Bitcoin etc). Compared to spot markets where the underlying asset changes ownership, in derivatives markets, traders trade contracts rather than the actual assets.

categories.name: Privacy Coins
categories.content: Cryptocurrencies designed primarily to function as digital cash or a store of value. Their architecture prioritizes the anonymity of the sender, receiver, and amount. They do not support general-purpose smart contracts or a dApp ecosystem.

categories.name: Bitcoin Fork
categories.content: A Bitcoin fork is a change to the underlying rules of the Bitcoin network that results in a split into a separate versions of the blockchain.

categories.name: Privacy Blockchain
categories.content: Programmable Layer 1 or Layer 2 networks that serve as platforms for dApps while prioritizing confidentiality. Unlike standard, general-purpose programmable blockchains like Ethereum, these networks have privacy preserved at the consensus or execution layer, enabling "private-by-default" or "opt-in private" smart contracts.

categories.name: DePIN
categories.content: DePIN refers to Decentralized Physical Infrastructure Networks which utilize blockchain and tokenized incentives to build real-world infrastructure across areas like wireless networks, storage, geolocation, transportation and energy.

categories.name: Chain Abstraction
categories.content: Chain abstraction is the concept of creating a seamless, unified user experience across multiple blockchains, allowing users and developers to interact with different chains without needing to manually bridge assets, switch networks, or handle chain-specific complexities.

categories.name: Trump-Affiliated
categories.content: This category includes tokens that are officially launched, endorsed, or held by Donald Trump or his immediate family. Only tokens with verifiable affiliation through official statements or reputable sources are included. Community-created tokens or projects that use Trump-related names or slogans without formal connection are excluded.

categories.name: RWA Protocol
categories.content: RWA Protocol refer to protocol that facilitates the tokenization of real-world assets.

categories.name: Privacy Infrastructure
categories.content: Protocols, networks, and developer tools designed to enable programmable privacy and confidential computation for decentralized applications. Unlike traditional 'Privacy Coins' which focus solely on transactional anonymity, these projects provide the infrastructure for encrypted smart contracts, private state management, and blind computation. They utilize advanced cryptography such as Zero-Knowledge Proofs (ZKPs), Fully Homomorphic Encryption (FHE), and Multi-Party Computation (MPC) to allow de

categories.name: Stablecoin Issuer
categories.content: Stablecoin issuers are protocols that create and manage stablecoins pegged to assets like fiat by using on-chain mechanisms such as collateralization, liquidity pools, or algorithmic supply adjustments.

categories.name: Cross-chain Communication
categories.content: Cross-chain communication allows different blockchain networks to interact and exchange data and assets.

categories.name: Zero Knowledge (ZK)
categories.content:
Zero-knowledge proof or Zero-knowledge protocol is a method by which one party (the prover) can prove to another party (the verifier) that a given statement is true while the prover avoids conveying any additional information apart from the fact that the statement is indeed true.

This category tracks cryptocurrency that utilises Zero Knowledge implementation to execute transactions, which may include smart contract execution, value transfer, and others.

categories.name: Optimism Superchain Ecosystem
categories.content: The Optimism Superchain is a unified network of chains built using the open-source OP Stack. This framework provides a standardized, modular architectural framework for creating Layer 2 chains that share a common security and communication layer.

categories.name: Crypto-backed Stablecoin
categories.content: A crypto-backed stablecoin is designed to maintain a stable value by being backed by a reserve of other cryptocurrencies.

categories.name: Layer 2 (L2)
categories.content: Layer 2s are off-chain vertical scaling solutions that run on top of Layer 1 blockchains like Ethereum to improve scalability, while maintaining the decentralization and security standards of the Layer 1.

categories.name: Oracle
categories.content: Oracles are used by protocols in their smart contracts in order to obtain external data. This allows the closed-off blockchain environment to communicate with data points on the outside world. For example, a protocol offering synthetic Nasdaq-listed stock on the blockchain will need to pull external data from the stock market. With an oracle, the protocol will be able to do so.

categories.name: Yield Farming
categories.content: Yield farming involves putting cryptocurrency into a DeFi protocol to collect interest on trading fees. Liquidity providers can profit by providing liquidity in DeFi protocols like Uniswap, utilizing assets that would otherwise sit idle on an exchange or hot wallet.

categories.name: x402 Ecosystem
categories.content: x402 is an open protocol that defines an internet-native micropayment rail using HTTP 402 and stablecoins. It allows automated clients and AI agents to pay directly for APIs, data, and compute on demand, enabling real-time, low-friction transactions without intermediaries.

categories.name: Binance Launchpool
categories.content: Tokens and coins launched on Binance Launchpool, a platform that allows crypto holders to earn new tokens by locking some of their existing assets.

categories.name: NFT
categories.content: Non-fungible tokens (NFTs) are collectible elements that represent something unique and therefore are not mutually interchangeable. In other words, no non-fungible token is the same. NFT creators can also encrypt details such as rich metadata or secure file links allowing people to create all sorts of digital assets which are verifiable such as videos and songs.

categories.name: Tokenized Commodities
categories.content: Tokenized Commodities refers to digital representation of commodities such as oil, gold, silver on a blockchain platform.

categories.name: Tokenized Gold
categories.content: Tokenized gold refers to digital representation of physical gold on a blockchain platform. These tokens are backed by an equivalent amount of real gold held in custody by the issuing institution.

categories.name: Automated Market Maker (AMM)
categories.content: Automated market makers (AMMs) make use of liquidity pools containing 2 or more assets, and prices are derived based on the proportion of each asset in that pool as well as the mathematical function used. Orders through an AMM are executed automatically via a smart contract that will calculate the trade prices algorithmically, including any slippage from the trade execution.

categories.name: Layer 0 (L0)
categories.content: Layer 0 is the foundational infrastructure upon which multiple Layer 1 blockchains can be built.

categories.name: Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG)
categories.content: A DAG-based blockchain is a type of distributed ledger that uses a graph-like structure instead of a linear chain, allowing faster and parallel transaction processing by linking each transaction to multiple previous ones.

categories.name: Solana Meme
categories.content: Meme coins native to the Solana network.

categories.name: Tokenized Treasury Bills (T-Bills)
categories.content: A Tokenized Treasury Bill (T-Bill) is a digital version of a U.S. government short-term debt security represented on a blockchain.

categories.name: Index Coop Defi Index
categories.content: The DeFi Pulse Index (DPI) is a capitalization-weighted index that tracks the performance of some of the largest protocols in the DeFi space.

categories.name: Gambling (GambleFi)
categories.content: GambleFi refers to decentralized gambling platforms and tokens leveraging blockchain technology and smart contracts.

categories.name: Gaming (GameFi)
categories.content: GameFi combines blockchain technology, gaming, and decentralized finance (DeFi), allowing players to earn cryptocurrency and NFT rewards while also offering true ownership and control over in-game assets.

categories.name: Prediction Markets
categories.content: A crypto prediction market is a marketplace where people can bet on the outcome of future events using crypto.

categories.name: Options
categories.content: Options refer to financial instruments that give holders the right, but not the obligation, to buy or sell a cryptocurrency at a predetermined price, known as the strike price, before a specific date, known as the expiry date.

categories.name: Quantum-Resistant
categories.content: Quantum-resistant projects are characterised by their use of post-quantum cryptographic algorithms (e.g., hash-based, lattice-based) to remain secure against potential attacks from future quantum computers.

categories.name: Crypto Card Issuer
categories.content: Tokens and cryptocurrencies representing platforms, centralized exchanges, or protocols that issue physical or virtual crypto debit and credit cards.

categories.name: Lending/Borrowing Protocols
categories.content: Lending/borrowing protocols allow users to offer crypto loans by staking their assets in them without the need for a bank account. Users are given rewards, usually in the form of the protocol’s native token.

categories.name: Launchpad
categories.content: Launchpad is a platform for crypto projects to hold Initial DEX Offerings (IDOs). Participants are able to gain early access to public and special token sales on the platform.

categories.name: Yield-Bearing Stablecoin
categories.content: Yield-bearing stablecoins are stablecoins that passively earn interest or yield for holders, either through DeFi lending, staking rewards, or real-world asset backing.

categories.name: Neobank
categories.content: A neobank is a digital-only bank that operates online or through mobile apps without physical branches.

categories.name: AI Agents
categories.content: An AI agent is a smart computer program that can act on its own to achieve goals.

categories.name: Payment Solutions
categories.content: Platforms or services that enable the acceptance and processing of cryptocurrency payments for goods and services.

categories.name: Wallets
categories.content: Crypto wallets are digital tools that allow you to interact with blockchain networks to store and manage cryptocurrencies.

categories.name: Binance HODLer Airdrops
categories.content: Binance HODLer Airdrops is an airdrop program by Binance. Users who subscribe to Simple Earn using BNB will receive airdropped tokens issued by projects with a large token circulating supply that intend to soon list on Binance.

categories.name: Metaverse
categories.content: The metaverse refers to a digital world where participants can interact with each other in a shared virtual reality.

categories.name: Data Availability
categories.content: Data availability on the blockchain ensures that all participants have the transaction data needed to verify blocks, even with resource limitations and scalability needs. Without it, independent verification crumbles, compromising the entire system. Data availability centric protocols aim to allow nodes to verify data availability more efficiently.

categories.name: Binance Launchpad
categories.content: Tokens and coins launched on Binance Launchpad, a platform that assists blockchain and crypto startups in raising funds.

categories.name: Play To Earn
categories.content: Play to Earn games are built on the blockchain, giving players full control over their gaming accounts and related assets, which they can sell on exchanges or secondary marketplaces.

categories.name: Binance Wallet IDO
categories.content: Tokens and coins launched on Binance Wallet IDO.

categories.name: Mobile Mining
categories.content: Mobile mining allows users to use a smartphone or mobile device to mine cryptocurrencies.

categories.name: SocialFi
categories.content: SocialFi combines social media and DeFi. It aims to bring a more decentralized and user-centric approach to social media platforms, allowing users to monetize their interactions and content directly.

categories.name: Frog-Themed
categories.content: Meme coins which are inspired by frogs.

categories.name: The Boy’s Club
categories.content: Meme coins which are inspired by The Boy's Club.

categories.name: Pump.fun Ecosystem
categories.content: Pump.fun Ecosystem consists of tokens launched via pump.fun.

categories.name: AI Framework
categories.content: An AI Framework/ AI agent framework is a set of tools, libraries, and methodologies designed to facilitate the development, management, and operation of AI agents.

categories.name: Storage
categories.content: Storage protocols allow users to store their data on the blockchain network in a decentralized manner. This negates the need for a centralized storage host such as Amazon, OneDrive, DropBox, and others. This removes the issue of a single point of failure. Decentralized servers make use of independent nodes which in turn use spare storage space on computers. Users are able to rent out their spare storage on  In exchange for storage space, users are able to use a storage protocol’s token to pay fo

categories.name: Decentralized Identifier (DID)
categories.content: Decentralized Identifier (DID) allows individuals or entities to create and manage their own identifiers independently of any centralized registry, identity provider, or intermediary.

categories.name: Yield-Bearing Tokens
categories.content: Yield-bearing tokens generate passive income for holders by accruing rewards or interest over time, typically through staking, lending, or yield-generating protocols.

categories.name: Rollup
categories.content: Rollup is a layer 2 solution that aggregates and processes transactions outside of a main blockchain, before submitting them as a single batch, to enhance scalability and reduce fees.

categories.name: Liquid Staking
categories.content: Liquid staking is a process in which users can stake their cryptocurrency tokens to earn rewards while maintaining the ability to use or trade those tokens in DeFi applications.

categories.name: US Treasury-backed Stablecoin
categories.content: A stablecoin that is 1:1 backed by U.S. Treasuries. This includes direct holdings of Treasury bills (T-bills), short-maturity Treasury notes (T-Notes), and repurchase agreements (repos) that are fully collateralized by U.S. Treasuries.

categories.name: Internet of Things (IOT)
categories.content: The Internet of Things (IoT) ecosystem consists of interconnected computing devices, with the ability to transfer data over a network without the need for any human interaction.

categories.name: PolitiFi
categories.content:
Political Finance (PolitiFi) are meme coins inspired by political figures.

Note: Most of these tokens have no official affiliation to any political figures.

categories.name: Analytics
categories.content: Projects that provide advanced insights and charting tools to track historical token prices, real-time trades, volume, and many more.

categories.name: AI Agent Launchpad
categories.content: Platforms that allow users to deploy and launch their own AI agents.

categories.name: AI Meme
categories.content: Meme coins related or inspired by AI. They either leverage AI-powered agents, are created using AI tools, or derive their concept from AI technologies and trends.

categories.name: Masternodes
categories.content: Masternodes are needed to verify new blocks in certain cryptocurrencies. However, unlike other nodes, they do not add new blocks to the network. In order to maintain a masternode, one would need to hold a certain amount of the protocol’s cryptocurrency, and it’s usually a significant amount. In return for operating a masternode, the operator is rewarded with the native currency.

categories.name: SideChain
categories.content: A sidechain is a separate blockchain that runs parallel to a main blockchain. It allows transactions and applications to operate independently to enhance scalability and functionality.

categories.name: Gaming Blockchains
categories.content: Gaming blockchains refer to blockchain platforms specialized in gaming.

categories.name: Morpho Ecosystem
categories.content: Vault tokens within the Morpho Protocol.

categories.name: Bittensor Subnets
categories.content: Subnets on Bittensor are specialized mini-networks dedicated to specific AI tasks. In each subnet, models (miners) compete to produce high-quality outputs, and their performance is evaluated by validators who assign rankings and allocate TAO rewards accordingly.

categories.name: Restaking
categories.content: Restaking allows users who have staked their tokens to participate in extending the underlying security of the base network to other protocols and networks.

categories.name: Bitcoin Sidechains
categories.content: Bitcoin Sidechains are designed to enhance the Bitcoin blockchain's capacity by creating a new layer that improves transaction processing speed by handling transactions off the primary chain.

categories.name: Dex Aggregator
categories.content: A DEX aggregator is designed to enhance the efficiency and accessibility of cryptocurrency trading. It searches across multiple decentralized exchanges (DEXs) to combine their liquidity, helping users avoid slippage on large orders, lower trading fees, and secure the best prices for tokens.

categories.name: EUR Stablecoin
categories.content: A EUR stablecoin is a type of cryptocurrency that is designed to maintain a stable value by being pegged to the Euro.

categories.name: Name Service
categories.content: Name Service is a decentralized naming system that allows users to map human-readable domain names to machine-readable information.

categories.name: Gaming Utility Token
categories.content: Gaming Utility Tokens provide holders with benefits such as making in-game purchases, accessing special content, participating in events, or earning rewards.

categories.name: Algorithmic Stablecoin
categories.content: An algorithmic stablecoin is a type of stablecoin that maintains its peg to a specific value, such as a fiat currency or other assets through algorithmic mechanisms. These mechanisms adjust the supply of the stablecoin based on market demand often by issuing more coins when the price is above the peg and buying back or burning coins when the price is below the peg.

categories.name: Airdropped Tokens by NFT Projects
categories.content: Airdropped tokens by NFT Projects refer to tokens distributed by NFT projects as part of their community engagement or ecosystem expansion initiatives. Airdrops are often tied to ownership of specific NFT collections or eligibility within certain user groups.

categories.name: IP Meme
categories.content: Meme projects tied to verifiable IP assets.

categories.name: Sports
categories.content:
These projects have introduced a new way for sports teams to engage with their fans and has made it easier for ordinary sports fans to show their support to their favorite teams and players. 
With Fan Tokens and NFTs, fans have the power to influence their favourite sports teams in minor decisions and enter an exclusive club of like-minded supporters and VIP benefits.

categories.name: Tokenized Treasury Bonds (T-Bonds)
categories.content: A Tokenized Treasury Bond (T-Bond) is a digital version of a U.S. government debt security represented on a blockchain.

categories.name: Liquid Staking Governance Tokens
categories.content: Liquid Staking Governance Tokens facilitate decision-making and policy formation in Liquid Staking Token Protocols, allowing holders to influence asset allocation and platform strategy.

categories.name: Parallelized EVM
categories.content: Parallel EVM refers to the capability of processing and executing multiple blockchain transactions simultaneously rather than in a sequential manner.

categories.name: DeFAI
categories.content: DeFAI or AIFI projects leverage AI to streamline and automate DeFi activities such as trading, staking, yield farming, market analysis, and investment optimization.

categories.name: Four.meme Ecosystem (BNB Memes)
categories.content: Four.meme Ecosystem consists of tokens launched via four.meme on BNB Chain.

categories.name: Liquid Restaking Governance Tokens
categories.content: Liquid Restaking Governance Tokens facilitate decision-making and policy formation in Liquid Restaking Token Protocols, allowing holders to influence asset allocation and platform strategy.

categories.name: BTCfi Protocol
categories.content: BTCfi Protocol refers to DeFi protocols built on or around the Bitcoin ecosystem. It aims to bring DeFi activities such as lending, borrowing, and yield farming to Bitcoin holders.

categories.name: VPN
categories.content: A Virtual Private Network (VPN) is a technology that creates an encrypted connection, allowing users to securely access and transmit data as though their devices were directly connected to a private network.

categories.name: MEV Protection
categories.content: MEV (Maximal Extractable Value) protection is a set of rules and mechanisms designed to prevent or mitigate the negative impacts of MEV in decentralized finance (DeFi) environments.

categories.name: Tokenized Stock
categories.content: Tokenized stock refers to digital representation of stock on a blockchain platform.

categories.name: Curve Ecosystem
categories.content: Interconnected platforms and services built around Curve Finance.

categories.name: Ondo Tokenized Assets
categories.content: Ondo Tokenized Assets are on-chain tokens that represent economic exposure to traditional stocks and ETFs, with each token typically backed 1:1 by the underlying security held in custody.

categories.name: Telegram Apps
categories.content: Applications built on the Telegram platform that integrate cryptocurrency or blockchain technology.

categories.name: Modular Blockchain
categories.content: A modular blockchain is a type of blockchain architecture that separates the core functions of a blockchain into distinct modules or layers. Each module is designed to handle specific tasks independently.

categories.name: Entertainment
categories.content: Projects that are specifically designed to be used within the entertainment sector, which may include areas such as music, film, gaming, and other forms of digital media.

categories.name: Gaming Governance Token
categories.content: Gaming Governance Token gives holders the right to participate in development and decision making process of the game.

categories.name: Buidlpad Launchpad
categories.content: Buidlpad is a launchpad that enables token sales with KYC-verified participants.

categories.name: RUB Stablecoin
categories.content: A RUB stablecoin is a type of cryptocurrency that is designed to maintain a stable value by being pegged to the Russian Ruble (RUB).

categories.name: Crypto-Backed Tokens
categories.content: Crypto-backed tokens are digital assets backed or collateralized by other cryptocurrencies. Stablecoins are excluded from this category and are classified separately under the Crypto-Backed Stablecoin category.

categories.name: Cat-Themed
categories.content: Meme coins which are inspired by cat.

categories.name: Binance Buildkey TGE
categories.content: The BuildKey TGE Model is a hybrid Token Generation Event (TGE) framework developed by Aspecta in collaboration with Binance Wallet.

categories.name: Murad Picks
categories.content: Tokens promoted by a memecoin KOL @MustStopMurad.

categories.name: Account Abstraction
categories.content: Account abstraction aims to simplify the way users interact with dApps by doing away with the complexities of gas fees and transaction management.

categories.name: RPG
categories.content: Role-playing game (RPG) is a video game genre where players control a single or group of character in a fictional world. RPG games typically include elements of storytelling, character development, exploration, quests, and inventory management.

categories.name: Synthetic Asset
categories.content: Synthetic assets are financial instruments that mimic the value of assets, such as stocks, bonds, commodities, or cryptocurrencies.

categories.name: Bridge Governance Tokens
categories.content: A bridge governance token is a type of cryptocurrency token that is used to manage and govern a blockchain bridge.

categories.name: Simulation Games
categories.content: Simulation game replicates real-world activities, offering players the opportunity to experience different skills or activities in a virtual environment.

categories.name: Ether.fi Ecosystem
categories.content: Interconnected platforms and services built around Ether.fi.

categories.name: Gaming Platform
categories.content: Gaming platform allows users to play, download, and manage video games. They often provide features like multiplayer matchmaking, community forums, and in-game purchases.

categories.name: Bridged-Tokens
categories.content: Bridged-tokens refers to a token that has been transferred or "bridged" from one blockchain to another, typically through the use of a blockchain bridge.

categories.name: Gaming Marketplace
categories.content: A platform where players can buy, sell, or trade in-game assets, currencies, or digital items.

categories.name: Seigniorage
categories.content: In the case of algorithmic stablecoins, seigniorage is generated when the stablecoin's value rises above its peg (e.g., $1). The protocol can then mint new tokens and sell them on the open market, generating revenue. This revenue is used to maintain the stablecoin's peg to its target value. If the stablecoin's value falls below its peg, the protocol can buy back tokens, reducing the supply and helping to restore the peg.

categories.name: Yield Aggregator
categories.content: Yield aggregators are protocols that collate multiple yield farms in a single place in order to ease the process of farming. With many new farms popping up on the market, it can be tedious for one to hop from farm to farm. However, with yield aggregators, that isn’t necessary as it’s done automatically in order to maximize the yield generated for users.

categories.name: Base Meme
categories.content: Meme coins native to the Base network.

categories.name: Rebase Tokens
categories.content: Rebase tokens are cryptocurrencies that are usually pegged to a certain value, and they control their prices by algorithmically adjusting their token’s circulating supply.

categories.name: Synthetic
categories.content: This category includes both synthetic asset issuers and the synthetic assets themselves. Synthetic assets are on-chain tokens that replicate the price behavior of another asset, whether it’s a fiat currency, commodity, or stock using smart contracts and price oracles.

categories.name: Stock market-themed
categories.content: Meme coins related to the stock market.

categories.name: TokenFi Launchpad
categories.content: TokenFi Launchpad is a platform for crypto projects to hold Initial DEX Offerings (IDOs). Participants are able to gain early access to public and special token sales on the platform.

categories.name: On-chain Gaming
categories.content: On-chain games refer to games where all components, including game logic, assets, interactions, and characteristics, are stored directly on the blockchain.

categories.name: Intent
categories.content: Intents are signed messages that simplify on-chain goals. They are handled by solvers to enhance user experiences, optimize transactions, and incentivize efficient execution paths.

categories.name: IP
categories.content: Intellectual property (IP) related crypto projects leverage blockchain technology to tokenize and manage intellectual property, enabling transparent ownership, automated royalties, and decentralized marketplaces for creators and investors.

categories.name: LSDFi
categories.content: Liquid Staking Derivatives Finance (LSDFi) combines the principles of liquid staking derivatives with traditional DeFi applications to offer enhanced financial opportunities and flexibility to cryptocurrency users.

categories.name: Card Games
categories.content: Crypto card games are digital card games that utilize blockchain technology allowing players to collect, trade, and play with unique digital cards often represented as NFTs.

categories.name: Midas Liquid Yield Tokens
categories.content: Midas Liquid Yield Tokens refer to liquid yield tokens issued by Midas and offered on https://midas.app/.

categories.name: Echo Launchpad
categories.content: Echo.xyz is a decentralized launchpad that enables early-stage project funding.

categories.name: Synthetic Issuer
categories.content: Issuer of synthetic asset.

categories.name: Insurance
categories.content: Decentralized insurance provides the infrastructure for members to buy cover, underwrite risk, assess claims, and build risk management businesses.

categories.name: BackedFi xStocks Ecosystem
categories.content: xStocks refers to the tokenized stocks and ETFs issued by BackedFi.

categories.name: Yield Optimizer
categories.content: Yield optimizer passively maximizing return by using an automated service that actively managing the fund.

categories.name: Decentralized Science (DeSci)
categories.content: Decentralized Science aims to leverage the blockchain and Web3 tools to create an open ecosystem to conduct, and disseminate scientific research.

categories.name: Avalanche L1
categories.content: Avalanche L1 are specialized sets of validators on Avalanche that allow the creation of customized independent networks with specific rules and governance to enable scalable and tailored blockchain solutions for various applications.

categories.name: Tradable Ecosystem

categories.content: Bridged WBNB refers to Wrapped BNB that has been transferred from its native blockchain to a different blockchain through "bridging".

categories.name: Bridged wstETH
categories.content: Bridged wstETH refers to Wrapped Staked ETH (wstETH) that has been transferred from its native blockchain to a different blockchain through "bridging".

categories.name: Binance-Peg Tokens
categories.content: Binance-Peg Tokens are wrapped versions of cryptocurrencies pegged by Binance on a 1:1 ratio.

categories.name: Wormhole Assets
categories.content: The Wormhole project is a bidirectional, decentralized SPL token bridge between Solana and EVM chains.

categories.name: Yearn Vault Tokens
categories.content: Yearn Vault Tokens (yVault Token), is a type of token that represents a user's share in a Yearn Vault.

categories.name: SRC-20
categories.content: The SRC-20 standard issues fungible tokens on the Bitcoin blockchain, attaching data via UTXOs for immutable and non-prunable storage.

categories.name: Index Coop Metaverse Index
categories.content: The Metaverse Index (MVI) is designed to capture the trend of entertainment, social activity and business moving to take place in virtual economies, powered by NFTs and blockchain technology.

categories.name: HyperXpad Launchpad
categories.content: HyperXpad Launchpad is a platform for crypto projects to hold Initial DEX Offerings (IDOs). Participants are able to gain early access to public and special token sales on the platform.

categories.name: Liquid Restaking Tokens
categories.content: Liquid Restaking Tokens are a liquid representation of restaking positions. Restaking enable users who have staked their tokens to extend the security of the base network to other protocols and networks.

categories.name: Friend.tech Ecosystem
categories.content: Interconnected platforms and services built around Friend.tech.

categories.name: Floor Protocol Tokens
categories.content: Floor Protocol is a fractionalized NFT platform. It allows the fragmentation of NFTs from prominent collections into μTokens, which can then be traded like any other cryptocurrency.

categories.name: BNB Chain Ecosystem
categories.content:
BNB Chain is an alternative blockchain that is similar to Ethereum, capable of hosting smart contracts and decentralized applications. It was launched by Binance in September 2020 as the Binance Smart Chain, and relaunched in Feburary 2022 as BNB Chain. BNB uses the Proof-of-Staked-Authority model which has allowed for low transaction fees and higher throughput. 

Compared to Ethereum which would usually cost hundreds to make a few transactions, BNB only charges less than a few dollars. BNB su

categories.name: Solana Ecosystem
categories.content: Solana is a general purpose blockchain similar to Ethereum. The underlying architecture is different, such that developers have to write applications using Rust instead of Solidity or Vyper. However, this may soon change with the introduction of the Neon EVM solution on Solana. End user applications as of now include decentralized finance (DeFi), non-fungible tokens (NFT), marketplaces, games, and more. One of its biggest features is its scalability in which Solana is able to process over 700,00

categories.name: Polygon Ecosystem
categories.content: Polygon, formerly known as Matic, was originally meant to be a Layer-2 scaling solution for Ethereum to improve transaction throughput and speed. However, it has since become more popular as a stand-alone blockchain, with its own native projects and decentralized applications. Major DeFi protocols such as Aave and Curve have also found second homes on Polygon. Unlike Ethereum, Polygon operates on Proof-of-Stake (PoS) in which network participants can stake the network’s native MATIC tokens to va

categories.name: Avalanche Ecosystem
categories.content: Avalanche is a smart contract platform that allows users to create their own multi-purpose blockchains or decentralized applications (dApps). Their mainnet was launched in September 2020 and has since become a major hub of activity for DeFi and NFTs. In 2021, they announced their Avalanche Rush incentives program to introduce more applications and to promote further growth of their ecosystem. The Avalanche chain is centered around 3 main blockchains - the P-Chain, X-Chain and C-Chain. The C-Chai

categories.name: Fantom Ecosystem
categories.content:
FANTOM is a new DAG-based smart contract platform that intends to solve the scalability issues of existing public distributed ledger technologies.
The platform intends to distinguish itself from the traditional block ledger-based storage infrastructure by attempting to employ an improved version of existing DAG-based protocols. Fantom adopts a new protocol known as the “Lachesis Protocol” to maintain consensus. This protocol is intended to be integrated into the Fantom Opera Chain. The aim is t

categories.name: TON Ecosystem
categories.content: Protocols built on The Open Network (TON), a blockchain designed using technology from Telegram.

categories.name: Gnosis Chain Ecosystem
categories.content: Formerly the xDai Chain, The Gnosis chain is a Layer 2 scaling solution for Ethereum but uses a different consensus algorithm - Proof of Stake (PoS) and Proof of Stake DAO (POSDAO). It is designed to be more efficient than Ethereum, with higher transaction throughput (70 transactions/second) and has a much lower transaction fee.

categories.name: Bittensor Ecosystem
categories.content: Interconnected platforms and services built around Bittensor.

categories.name: Harmony Ecosystem
categories.content: Harmony is a blockchain platform that is designed to act as a bridge between scalability and interoperability. Its focus is on processing speed and validation of blocks. It can be used to create decentralized applications (DApps), and is currently focused on random state sharding. This will then allow the creation of blocks within seconds.

categories.name: Kaia Ecosystem
categories.content: Kaia is a blockchain platform developed by Ground X, a subsidiary of Kakao. It emphasizes scalability, user-friendliness, and enterprise integration for decentralized applications. The Klay token is used within the ecosystem for all platform transactions, as well as other blockchain applications.

categories.name: Near Protocol Ecosystem
categories.content: NEAR is a sharded, developer-friendly, proof-of-stake public blockchain. It is designed to compete with Ethereum by providing a similar experience with decentralized applications and smart contracts, but with lower fees and higher throughput. The blockchain’s native token, NEAR, is used to pay for transactions and storing data on the blockchain. Smart contract developers receive a portion of the transaction fees generated by their contracts, while the remainder is burnt. This creates deflationar

categories.name: Berachain Ecosystem
categories.content: Berachain is an EVM-compatible blockchain built on Proof-of-Liquidity consensus.

categories.name: Scroll Ecosystem
categories.content: Scroll is a Layer 2 network that aims to extend Ethereum's capabilities through zero knowledge (ZK) tech and EVM compatibility.

categories.name: Cosmos Ecosystem
categories.content: Cosmos focuses on blockchain interoperability, working towards the vision of building the “Internet of Blockchains.”

categories.name: Polkadot Ecosystem
categories.content: Polkadot is a blockchain protocol designed to support multiple purpose-built blockchains under one unified network. Polkadot’s infrastructure begins with the relay chain, which acts as the central chain. Each chain that runs on Polkadot is called a parachain as they run parallel to the main relay chain, and is built on top of the relay chain. Besides parachains, projects can participate in the Polkadot ecosystem for a shorter fixed period of time through parathreads. Blockchains built on top of

categories.name: Ronin Ecosystem
categories.content: Protocols that are built on the Ronin network, an EVM-compatible blockchain designed for games.

categories.name: Manta Network Ecosystem
categories.content: Protocols that are built on the Manta network, an EVM-compatible ZK-application platform.

categories.name: Terra Ecosystem
categories.content: Terra is a blockchain network that builds on the Tendermint consensus (Proof-of-Stake) and the Cosmos SDK toolkit. Terra’s network token is LUNA which powers the entire ecosystem. Unlike most blockchains, Terra’s ecosystem includes a native algorithmic stablecoin, TerraUSD (UST). A decentralized network with its own decentralized currency is a very attractive thesis for both users and developers. More dApps are being built on Terra, especially DeFi protocols which are now commonly known as TeFi.

categories.name: ZetaChain Ecosystem
categories.content: Zetachain is a Proof of Stake (PoS) blockchain built on the Cosmos SDK and Tendermint PBFT consensus engine. It is designed to facilitate fast transactions and instant finality across interconnected blockchains.

categories.name: Neon Ecosystem
categories.content: Neon is an on-chain solution that brings native Ethereum Virtual Machine (EVM) dApps to the Solana network without any reconfiguration.

categories.name: Kadena Ecosystem
categories.content: Kadena is a scalable Proof of Work blockchain built using the Pact smart contract language. It aims to build a scalable and developer-friendly public blockchain with a level of security on-par with Bitcoin.

categories.name: Apex Chain Ecosystem
categories.content: Apex Chain is a gas-free blockchain, powered by the Omnia token.
